q-64648.name: Question 1
q-64648.problem:
The position $y(t),$ measured in meters, of a particle oscillating with periodically forced harmonic motion without damping is governed by the equation

$$
{y}^{″}+4y=\operatorname{cos}⁡pt-\operatorname{sin}⁡pt,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Which value of the parameter $p$ causes the oscillator to resonate?
q-64648.worked_solution:
The equation of forced harmonic motion without damping is

$$
{y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=4\,⟹\,\omega =2.
$$

Thus, we have

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡2t.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency $p$ of the external periodic force $f(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡pt-\operatorname{sin}⁡pt$ coincides with the frequency of the complementary solution, which is $\omega =2.$

Therefore, the oscillator experiences resonance when $p=2.$

Question 1
?

The position y(t), measured in meters, of a particle oscillating with periodically forced harmonic motion without damping is governed by the equation

y″+4y=cos⁡pt−sin⁡pt,

where t>0 is the time, in seconds. Which value of the parameter p causes the oscillator to resonate?

a
p=6
b
p=2
c
p=4
d
p=2
e
p=1
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The equation of forced harmonic motion without damping is

y″+ω2y=f(t).

The complementary solution yc here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

yc=Acos⁡ωt+Bsin⁡ωt,

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency p of the external periodic force f(t)=cos⁡pt−sin⁡pt coincides with the frequency of the complementary solution, which is ω=2.

Therefore, the oscillator experiences resonance when p=2.

q-343662.html:
Question 4
?

The position y(t), measured in meters, of a particle oscillating with periodically forced harmonic motion without damping is governed by the equation y″+y=−4sin⁡pt,

where t>0 is the time, in seconds. Which value of the parameter p causes the oscillator to resonate?

a
p=12
b
p=1
c
p=22
d
p=2
e
p=2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The equation of forced harmonic motion without damping is

y″+ω2y=f(t).

The complementary solution yc here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

yc=Acos⁡ωt+Bsin⁡ωt,

where A and B are arbitrary constants of integration.

In our case, ω2=1⟹ω=1.

Thus, we have

yc=Acos⁡t+Bsin⁡t.

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency p of the external periodic force f(t)=−4sin⁡pt coincides with the frequency of the complementary solution, which is ω=1.

Therefore, the oscillator experiences resonance when p=1.

q-343770.name: Question 5
q-343770.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force
$f(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t).$
Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position $y(t)?$

I. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t+ϕ)+\frac{4}{5}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+\frac{1}{5}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)$

II. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t+ϕ)+\frac{4}{5}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+\frac{1}{5}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)$

III. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)+\frac{1}{5}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
q-343770.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega .$

The external force is $f(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t),$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $5.$ Therefore,
$\omega =5.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

1\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t+ϕ)$

2\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t+ϕ)$

3\. ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega $ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega =5$ into the differential equation, ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[(10D-25Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-(10C+25Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)]+25t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ 10D\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-10C\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=\frac{4}{5}$ and $D=\frac{1}{5}.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\frac{4}{5}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+\frac{1}{5}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t).
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

1\. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t+ϕ)+\frac{4}{5}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+\frac{1}{5}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)$

2\. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t+ϕ)+\frac{4}{5}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+\frac{1}{5}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)$

3\. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)+\frac{4}{5}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+\frac{1}{5}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)$

Only solutions I and II match the forms above.
Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".

q-343770.html:
Question 5
?

A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force f(t)=2cos⁡(5t)−8sin⁡(5t). Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position y(t)?

  1. y=Rcos⁡(5t+ϕ)+45tcos⁡(5t)+15tsin⁡(5t)
  2. y=Rsin⁡(5t+ϕ)+45tcos⁡(5t)+15tsin⁡(5t)
  3. y=Acos⁡(5t)+Bsin⁡(5t)+15tcos⁡(5t)
Note that A, B, R, and ϕ are constants.

a
I only
b
II only
c
I and III only
d
III only
e
I and II only
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency ω.

The external force is f(t)=2cos⁡(5t)−8sin⁡(5t), which is sinusoidal with frequency 5. Therefore, ω=5.

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

  1. yc=Rcos⁡(ωt+ϕ)=Rcos⁡(5t+ϕ)

  2. yc=Rsin⁡(ωt+ϕ)=Rsin⁡(5t+ϕ)

  3. yc=Acos⁡ωt+Bsin⁡ωt=Acos⁡(5t)+Bsin⁡(5t)

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency ω duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by t and take a resonant particular solution of the form yp(t)=t(Ccos⁡(5t)+Dsin⁡(5t)).

By substituting the particular solution and ω=5 into the differential equation, y″+ω2y=f(t), we get [(10D−25Ct)cos⁡(5t)−(10C+25Dt)sin⁡(5t)]+25t(Ccos⁡(5t)+Dsin⁡(5t))=2cos⁡(5t)−8sin⁡(5t)10Dcos⁡(5t)−10Csin⁡(5t)=2cos⁡(5t)−8sin⁡(5t)

Equating coefficients, C=45 and D=15.

So, the particular solution is yp(t)=45tcos⁡(5t)+15tsin⁡(5t).

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

  1. y=Rcos⁡(5t+ϕ)+45tcos⁡(5t)+15tsin⁡(5t)

  2. y=Rsin⁡(5t+ϕ)+45tcos⁡(5t)+15tsin⁡(5t)

  3. y=Acos⁡(5t)+Bsin⁡(5t)+45tcos⁡(5t)+15tsin⁡(5t)

Only solutions I and II match the forms above. Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".
